capture.metricsSource: Auxiliary sampler: the isolated guest's /proc/stat, /proc/meminfo and /proc/pressure/*
capture.snapshotSource: Actual Bullseye state.json; every distinct evaluatedAt/version, including same-version heartbeats
capture.transitionSource: Actual Bullseye state.json; first observation of each version
capture.logSource: Allowlisted Bullseye stdout with guest-side observation timestamps; source-workload names are consistently aliased where marked
capture.transitionTiming: atMs is the first capture time; sinceMs is the agent state-transition time; evaluatedAtMs is the latest evaluation time
capture.evidenceMeaning: evidence is diagnostic reasoning and may be retained; observations.metrics are current agent telemetry
capture.freshnessMeaning: Observation freshness is independent of severity. evaluatedAt is an evaluation heartbeat, not a successful file-write time.
notes: Recorded genuine two-vCPU Linux guest; not live monitoring or a production capacity benchmark.
The reviewed original Bullseye defaults are unchanged, including CPU, memory, PSI, sampling and attribution-refresh settings.
The recording includes agent startup; startup stdout retains its actual position in the replay timeline.
Metrics and snapshots retain actual values; no states, current telemetry or workload attribution are synthesized.
Repeated evaluation snapshots with the same version are retained; version increments describe semantic diagnostic changes.
The source-workload name capture-memory-workload is presented as memory-worker; other names use anonymous workload aliases.
Expired observation metrics remain absent. A stopped agent requires a consumer heartbeat-age check even if its last file says FRESH.
